name: python-socketio-parameterized-namespace-routes
instr:
Applications can register class-based synchronous and asyncio server and client handlers for parameterized namespace routes while retaining concrete routing context. Routed handlers coexist predictably with exact and catch-all registrations and remain visible through administrator instrumentation.

`NamespaceRoute` accepts absolute templates with literal and named segments, exposes `template` and `parameter_names`, and rejects malformed or duplicate declarations with `InvalidNamespaceRoute`, a ValueError whose `template` identifies the input. Complete-namespace matches return independent decoded parameter mappings and the concrete namespace in `NamespaceMatch` without mutating the route. Resolution prefers exact registrations, then parameterized routes ordered by literal-segment count and depth, then catch-all; indistinguishable routes raise `NamespaceRouteConflict`, a ValueError with `first_template` and `second_template`. Server and client registrations return a `NamespaceRegistration` exposing effective `route` and `active` state, and replacement or removal atomically preserves one owner while existing bindings retain their handler and new dispatches use replacements. Malformed or conflicting attempts preserve the prior active owner in routing and administrator views. Every synchronous and asynchronous server or client invocation sees only its concrete `route_params` and `route_namespace`, including through nesting, concurrency, awaits, completion, failure, and cancellatio
